hypothesis: The design now deadlocks during the first few fetches: every benchmark freezes with imem_addr=0x0000000c, retired count=0, and halted=0 until the simulation-timeout. The identical frozen PC (0x0c, i.e. the 4th word) across crc32, array_sum and the ooo test shows the front-end is held on a pending fetch/handshake that never completes rather than a datapath value error. The wait-state/hold logic added in the last round (imem-ready gating and dmem-wait overlap in if_stage/mem_stage/rv32i5) never releases: the stage asserts imem_valid for the pending word but either deasserts/re-toggles the request or requires a ready/response handshake the top level never produces under the single-cycle model, so imem_addr stays pinned and the pipeline makes zero forward progress. Because no instruction can retire, dbg_retire_valid never pulses, all dbg_reg reads return 0, no ECALL can commit to set halted, and the teacher TB reaches its cycle cap (whole run >20 s) for every test — exactly the observed simulation_timeout with x17=0, x18=0, DMEM untouched and retired=0.
constraints: Preserve every top-level rv32i5 port name/width and the frozen stage/cache/branch_predictor port lists exactly.

Single-cycle memory model: imem/dmem must be serviced the same cycle the request is presented; do not introduce a multi-cycle wait-state or a ready/response handshake that the teacher TB is not required to satisfy.
imem_addr[1:0] must remain 00; during reset imem_addr=0 and dmem_valid=0, and no access issued while rst_n low.
Bubble/flush only via valid bits, never by holding a stage indefinitely; load-use holds PC/IF-ID/ID-EX for exactly one cycle, no permanent stall.
Halt/exit_code set only in WB for a committed ECALL; once halted freeze fetch and stop retiring. Do not modify TB, spec, or scoring.
Do not break the branch-predictor/dcache interfaces or the dbg_* observables wiring already fixed.
